english: Should Moltke take part in the shooting drills?
topic: General mathematical-philosophical remarks contrasting geometers and analysts, citing Jacobi and Weierstrass as true geometers in the calculus of variations and Clebsch and Hesse as formalist analysts, and stressing the value of general ideas over details.

triage.modern_statement: This is not a mathematical question. It is a rhetorical analogy. 'Moltke' almost certainly means Field Marshal Helmuth von Moltke the Elder, the Prussian chief of the General Staff and strategist. Asking whether the supreme strategist should join the rank-and-file shooting drills makes the page's point by analogy: a mathematician of general, 'geometric' ideas (Hilbert's examples are Jacobi and Weierstrass) need not do the detailed formal calculation associated with the formalist analysts (Clebsch, Hesse). In modern terms it is a methodological remark that general ideas matter more than technical details. Nothing about it can be proved or disproved.
triage.answered_by: Not applicable. It is a rhetorical, methodological question with no mathematical content to resolve.

evidence.claim: Helmuth von Moltke the Elder was Chief of Staff of the Prussian General Staff from 1857 to 1871 and of the Great General Staff from 1871 to 1888. He is the obvious 'Moltke' for a German writer of Hilbert's era, and is known as a strategist rather than a field soldier.
He is regarded as one of the great strategists of the nineteenth century, which fits his use here as a symbol of 'general ideas' set against the 'details' of drill.

The contrast between analysts and geometers, with Jacobi and Weierstrass described in terms of method and style, was a standard topic in the German mathematical culture of the time. Klein's lectures on 19th-century mathematics discuss it, including Jacobi's 1831 thesis that geometric and analytic methods share the same principle.
